extracted.intended_audience: covered entities subject to HHS Section 1557 (health programs and activities), health care providers, insurers, compliance officers, and Section 1557 coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for Section 1557-related employee training and for providing Notices of Nondiscrimination and Notices of Availability (language access/auxiliary aids) for health programs and activities covered by HHS. Includes content, timing, format, language-translation, accessibility, and alternative compliance options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training timing and scope (§92.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must begin training its relevant employees no later than 30 days after a covered entity implements its policies and procedures required by §92.8 and no later than 300 days after the effective date of the part; §92.9(b)(4) defines 'relevant employees' for the section (including permanent and temporary employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to expand the required training scope beyond the Section 1557 Policies and Procedures in §92.9, but encourages covered entities to provide additional civil rights and nondiscrimination training (e.g., interactive Q&A formats, engaging people with lived experience). Covered entities must retain training documentation for the requisite time period (modified from 'maintain' to 'retain').

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Nondiscrimination required recipients and basic obligation (§92.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Nondiscrimination relating to their health programs and activities to participants, beneficiaries, enrollees, applicants of their health programs and activities, and members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice is a critical proactive civil rights communication to inform individuals of rights (including how to access interpreters/auxiliary aids and how to file a grievance). OCR will provide a sample Notice of Nondiscrimination; covered entities may combine this notice with other statutory notices if the combined notice clearly informs individuals of their civil rights under Section 1557 and meets §92.10(a)(1) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Notice of Nondiscrimination (including Section 1557 Coordinator contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Nondiscrimination must include the components listed at §92.10(a)(1), including a clear explanation of rights and contact information for the Section 1557 Coordinator, as set forth in §92.10(a)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to require inclusion of ADA Coordinator contact information because the regulation is limited to section 1557 and not all covered entities are subject to the ADA. While OCR will provide a model notice and may translate it, the rule does not mandate translations of the Notice of Nondiscrimination into a set number of languages; however, translations may still be required when necessary to ensure meaningful access per §92.201.

rubrics_metrics.name: When and where Notice of Nondiscrimination must be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires the Notice of Nondiscrimination to be provided annually and upon request (as opposed to the 2016 Rule's 'significant communications'), and to be posted prominently on websites and in physical locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR balanced burden concerns with the need to inform people of their rights. Posting in physical locations and providing upon request ensures access is not dependent on internet access. Covered entities may be asked to provide notices in locations where frontline employees can see them and to ensure visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posted notice accessibility: font requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Posted notices must be in a sans serif font, no smaller than 20-point font (§92.10(a)(2)(iv) revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR finalized the 20-point sans serif requirement to ensure visibility and accessibility for individuals with low vision. Commenters had recommended at least 18-point; OCR set 20-point as the standard for posted notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of sex-discrimination parenthetical
rubrics_metrics.description: The parenthetical for sex discrimination in §92.10(a)(1)(i) has been revised to read 'consistent with the scope of sex discrimination described at §92.101(a)(2)' to ensure inclusion of sexual orientation, gender identity, and pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This edit aligns the Notice language with §92.101(a)(2) and with edits made to the Nondiscrimination Policy required by §92.8(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Reasonable steps" standard for meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.10(a)(1)(iii) was revised to replace 'necessary' with 'a reasonable step' consistent with §92.201(a), which states '[a] covered entity must take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to each individual with limited English proficiency...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies the governing standard for providing meaningful access—entities are required to take reasonable steps rather than an absolute 'necessary' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Availability content requirement (§92.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Availability must, at minimum, state that the covered entity provides language assistance services and appropriate auxiliary aids and services free of charge in its health programs and activities, when necessary for compliance with section 1557 or the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice informs individuals of the availability of language assistance and auxiliary aids/services and is foundational to ensuring meaningful access and reducing health disparities for persons with LEP and persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Availability language and alternate-format requirements (§92.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Availability must be provided in English and at least the 15 most common non-English languages spoken by individuals with LEP of the relevant State or States, and in alternate formats for individuals with disabilities who require auxiliary aids and services to ensure effective communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR selected the top-15-language State/States formula after considering census data and burden. OCR will provide translations of the model Notice of Availability in the top 15 languages for each State at www.hhs.gov/1557. Covered entities must still take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to all individuals with LEP even if the individual's language is not among the top 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: When and where Notice of Availability must be provided (§92.11(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Availability must be provided on an annual basis to participants, beneficiaries, enrollees (including late and special enrollees), and applicants, and upon request at any time; it must also be provided online (when applicable) and in a clear and prominent physical location where it is reasonable to expect individuals seeking services to be able to read or hear the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §92.11(c)(5) lists specific electronic and written communications that the Notice of Availability must accompany; OCR sought comment on EOB inclusion and balancing burden with coverage. Posting online and physically provides multiple access channels for populations with disparate internet access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific documents requiring Notice of Availability (including billing/good faith estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.11(c)(5) provides a list of specific electronic and written communications that the Notice of Availability must accompany; §92.11(c)(5)(ix) specifically requires including communications related to cost and payment of care, including medical billing and collections materials and good faith estimates required by section 2799B-6 of the Public Health Service Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR added billing-related documents to ensure individuals (including those with LEP/disabilities) can understand financial communications and exercise billing dispute rights. The list prioritizes critical health care documents while balancing entity burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative/optional compliance methods for Notice of Availability (§92.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.11(d) provides alternative, optional methods by which a covered entity may be deemed in compliance with §92.11(a), including opt-out mechanisms and documentation approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options are optional (not required). OCR allows covered entities to permit an individual to opt-out or to document an individual's primary language and appropriate auxiliary aids and services. OCR will provide oversight of opt-outs and technical assistance. Entities may choose delayed applicability or electronic-only approaches, but OCR declined requests to limit or remove these alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining Notice of Availability and Notice of Nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may choose to integrate the Notice of Availability into their Notice of Nondiscrimination; §92.11(c)(5)(i) requires the Notice of Availability be provided with the Notice of Nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR appreciates that combining notices may reduce burden; however, §92.11(c)(5) requires the Notice of Availability to be included with a list of important health care documents to ensure notice of language assistance rights reaches people in contexts critical for meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation method for languages and scope for national entities
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR adopted a State-or-States top-15 languages formula (aggregated across the State(s) in which the entity operates) to determine required translation languages; OCR declines to adopt a county-level or hybrid percentage/absolute-number threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR found the State/States top-15 approach covers a significant majority (over 93%) of individuals with LEP for national entities. OCR will monitor the area and coordinate with CMS as appropriate. Entities remain obligated to take reasonable steps for those not covered by the top-15 list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and effective-communication obligations apply to notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful access (§92.201) and effective communication (§92.202) requirements apply to the Notice of Availability and Notice of Nondiscrimination so that notices must be provided in alternate formats or via auxiliary aids/services when necessary to ensure effective communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to require specific additional formats (e.g., mandatory ASL or audio for every notice) at this time, but emphasizes that existing obligations under §92.201/§92.202 (and section 504/section 1557) will typically require providing the notice in alternate formats or via auxiliary aids/services as necessary (e.g., large print, screen reader–accessible, audio, qualified reader). Best practices include posting where frontline employees can see it and proactively asking individuals about communication barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR-provided model notices and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will provide a sample Notice of Nondiscrimination and has provided translations of the model Notice of Availability in the top 15 languages in each State at www.hhs.gov/1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing model notices and translations is intended to reduce burden on covered entities. Jurisdictions may still require additional languages; covered entities may provide more translations than required.
